- When sentiment is positive (≥0.25) in recent days, model tends to underpredict early spikes; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for the first 5–7 days after sentiment shift.
- Model consistently overestimates mid-term (15–25 day) prices after recent spikes; reduce forecast by 1–3% for days 15–25 if sentiment was neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.00) for 3+ consecutive days, model often undercorrects; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for days 10–20 to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model exhibits strong lag in correcting downward trends; if true price drops below 65% of recent high, forecast should be adjusted downward by 1–2% per day until price stabilizes.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate later months (days 20–30) when sentiment is weak; reduce forecast by 1–3% for days 20–30 if sentiment is ≤0.10.
- If sentiment peaks early (e.g., day 1–3) and model responds with a sharp spike, then correct by 1–2% in the next 3–5 days to avoid overshoot.
- Mean reversion is often delayed by 5–7 days; if true price is below 10% of recent 18-day average, forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.
